correctness.rationale: All vertices have even degree and the closed-neighborhood minority rule flips exactly when the matching-neighbor count is at least half the degree. Equal-color-edge energy is nonincreasing; any monochromatic triangle admits a strictly improving peripheral flip, excluding all higher-energy recurrent states. In minimum energy each triangle is one of three patterns; periphery flips form P3 and hub flips connect the two products only at all-mixed corners, showing one recurrent component of size 2*3^m. Symmetric neutral flips give the uniform law, from which the hub-flip rate follows by counting. Conditioning stationary paths to a hub layer and applying a crossing union bound proves the mixing-time lower bound. Scripts check all finite transitions m<=4 and the entire product transition graph m<=5, without treating finite checks as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The specific mathematically motivated question from asynchronous minority dynamics is whether reaching the sole recurrent class entails rapid equilibration. The natural bouquet of m frustrated triangles has one communicating ground-state manifold, yet its hub changes only at a 2^m corner subset of 3^m local patterns. This exact phase bottleneck produces exponential mixing obstruction while the energy-minimizing region is connected. It captures a structural topology-dependent phenomenon beyond a routine static count and is relevant to finite-state stochastic cellular automata and zero-temperature anti-coordination.
